title_en: Yu Shanlan v. ICBC Xuanwu Sub-branch and ICBC Beijing Branch — dispute over unjust enrichment
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 92 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, when a financial enterprise, in issuing service integrated circuit cards related to the administrative management duties of administrative organs, violates the fee management measures and charges parties fees beyond the cost of production, it constitutes unjust enrichment.
keywords_en: civil; unjust enrichment dispute; second instance; intermediate people's court; Beijing; natural person; financial institution; General Principles of the Civil Law; whether charging for card replacement constitutes unjust enrichment; legal basis for fee standards; retroactivity of regulations; reversal of judgment; replacement of Peony Transportation IC card; charging a fee of 100 yuan; failure to report fee standards for approval; ICBC Beijing Branch unjust enrichment dispute
full_text_en:
Yu Shanlan v. Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Beijing Xuanwu Sub-branch and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Beijing Branch — dispute over unjust enrichment

【Ruling Summary】

According to Article 92 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, where a financial enterprise, when issuing service-oriented integrated circuit cards related to the administrative management functions of administrative organs, charges fees beyond the cost of the card in violation of the fee management measures, such conduct constitutes unjust enrichment.

Plaintiff: Yu Shanlan, male, 41 years old, journalist of China Industry and Commerce News, residing in Zaoyuan Residential Community, Daxing District, Beijing.

Defendant: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Beijing Xuanwu Sub-branch, domiciled at: South Binhe Road, Outside Guang'anmen, Xuanwu District, Beijing.
Person in charge: Guo Zhigang, Sub-branch Manager.

Defendant: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Beijing Branch, domiciled at: Fuxingmen South Street, Xicheng District, Beijing.
Person in charge: Li Xiaopeng, Branch Manager.

The plaintiff, Yu Shanlan, filed an action with the Xuanwu District People's Court of Beijing against the defendants, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Beijing Xuanwu Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as "ICBC Xuanwu Sub-branch") and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Beijing Branch (hereinafter referred to as "ICBC Beijing Branch"), concerning a dispute over unjust enrichment.

The plaintiff, Yu Shanlan, alleged: When the plaintiff went to the Baizhifang Savings Office under the defendant ICBC Xuanwu Sub-branch to obtain a replacement Peony Traffic IC Card, the savings office charged the plaintiff RMB 100 in accordance with the fee standard established by the defendant ICBC Beijing Branch. After the incident, the plaintiff learned that this fee standard, implemented by all ICBC branches in Beijing, had not been approved by the competent price authorities and violated Articles 7, 8, and 9 of the Measures for the Administration of the Application and Charges of Integrated Circuit Cards. Charging fees according to this standard to persons applying for replacement Peony Traffic IC Cards constitutes an act of unjust enrichment without legal basis. The plaintiff requested the court to order ICBC Xuanwu Sub-branch to return the RMB 100 and the interest thereon up to the date of judgment, to order ICBC Beijing Branch to immediately cease implementing the fee standard it had formulated, to submit the fee standard for replacement Peony Traffic IC Cards to the Beijing price authority for approval in accordance with the relevant provisions, and to bear the litigation costs.

The defendant ICBC Xuanwu Sub-branch argued: Since the plaintiff also named the defendant's superior, ICBC Beijing Branch, as a co-defendant, the defense of this defendant shall be based on the defense of its superior.

The defendant ICBC Beijing Branch argued: The Peony Traffic IC Card is a bank card business jointly launched by this defendant and the Beijing Traffic Management Bureau in 1999, targeting motor vehicle drivers in Beijing. The card contains driving file information of motor vehicle drivers, traffic violation fine information, and has other functions with high technological content. At the inception of this business, this defendant undertook the development of the entire system and the investment in software and hardware, distributing over 3.2 million cards free of charge over several years, with total investment of approximately RMB 100 million. In 1999, there were no laws or regulations governing fees for replacement or exchange of integrated circuit cards. Given the high system development and maintenance costs for this high-tech product and the high cost of card production, this defendant, in accordance with Article 6 of the Price Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "commodity prices and service prices, except those subject to government-guided prices or government-set prices in accordance with Article 18 of this Law, shall be subject to market-adjusted prices and shall be independently set by business operators in accordance with this Law," and considering the cost situation of the Peony Traffic IC Card at that time, established the standard of charging RMB 100 for replacement or exchange of cards. The Measures for the Administration of the Application and Charges of Integrated Circuit Cards, on which the plaintiff relies, came into effect on September 28, 2001. This measure does not stipulate how fees for integrated circuit cards prior to its implementation should be adjusted, and therefore it does not have retroactive effect on the pricing and charging of integrated circuit cards before its implementation. This defendant established the fee standard for replacement of Peony Traffic IC Cards and charged accordingly in the absence of any legal or regulatory provisions. This clearly does not satisfy the definition of unjust enrichment under Article 92 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and does not constitute unjust enrichment. Accordingly, the defendant disagreed with the plaintiff's claims.

The Xuanwu District People's Court of Beijing found through trial:

On July 30, 2003, the plaintiff, Yu Shanlan, lost his Peony Traffic IC Card and needed to renew his motor vehicle driver's license. He therefore went to the Baizhifang Savings Office under the defendant ICBC Xuanwu Sub-branch to apply for a replacement Peony Traffic IC Card. The savings office presented to Yu Shanlan a Peony Traffic IC Card Collection (Replacement) Notice Form No. 3728814, prepared by the defendant ICBC Beijing Branch, which stated: "I voluntarily apply for the Peony Traffic IC Card and guarantee to comply with all usage provisions of the Peony Traffic IC Card financial services." Yu Shanlan signed below this statement and paid RMB 100 as a replacement card fee. The savings office issued him a Peony Traffic IC Card with card number 0000010270008317429. Yu Shanlan believed that the fees charged by the two defendants for the replacement card had no legal basis and constituted unjust enrichment, so he filed this lawsuit. During mediation, both parties maintained their positions.

Further investigation revealed: The Peony Traffic IC Card was launched and issued by the defendant ICBC Beijing Branch in 1999. The card contains driving file information of motor vehicle drivers, traffic violation fine information, and also has functions such as finance, electronic wallet, and gas payment. The Measures for the Administration of the Application and Charges of Integrated Circuit Cards were formulated by the State Planning Commission, the National Golden Card Project Coordination Leading Group, the Ministry of Finance, and the People's Bank of China on September 28, 2001.

The above facts were confirmed by the statements of both parties, the Peony Traffic IC Card Collection (Replacement) Notice Form of ICBC Beijing Branch, and other evidence.

The Xuanwu District People's Court of Beijing held:

Article 92 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "If a person obtains unjust benefits without a legal basis, causing loss to another person, he shall return the unjust benefits to the person who suffered the loss."

Thus, unjust enrichment refers to benefits obtained by a person through causing loss to another's property, without a legal basis such as law or contract. Article 44, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A lawfully formed contract shall become effective upon its formation." Article 60, Paragraph 1 provides: "The parties shall fully perform their obligations as agreed." In this case, after losing his Peony Traffic IC Card, the plaintiff Yu Shanlan went to the savings office under the defendant ICBC Xuanwu Sub-branch to apply for a replacement card. The replacement card notice form presented to him by the savings office stated: "I voluntarily apply for the Peony Traffic IC Card and guarantee to comply with all usage provisions of the Peony Traffic IC Card financial services." After Yu Shanlan signed to confirm, the savings office, in accordance with the regulations of the defendant ICBC Beijing Branch, charged Yu Shanlan RMB 100 as a replacement card fee and issued a replacement Peony Traffic IC Card. The above conduct of both parties constituted a service contract relationship established on a voluntary basis. Both parties in this case are persons with full civil capacity, and the entire transaction process reflected the true intention of both parties. After Yu Shanlan signed the replacement card notice form, the parties reached a lawful and valid contract. Subsequently, Yu Shanlan's payment of RMB 100 and the savings office's issuance of the replacement card constituted the lawful performance of the contract by both parties. The replacement card conduct did not violate mandatory legal provisions and was consistent with public order and good customs. The savings office charged Yu Shanlan RMB 100 as a replacement card fee based on the lawful and valid contract reached by both parties; therefore, this amount was not unjust enrichment. Yu Shanlan's claim requesting ICBC Xuanwu Sub-branch to return the RMB 100 as unjust enrichment and pay corresponding interest up to the date of judgment lacked factual basis and legal support and was not upheld.

Article 5 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "The lawful civil rights and interests of citizens and legal persons shall be protected by law, and no organization or individual may infringe upon them." In 1999, the defendant ICBC Beijing Branch, together with the Beijing Traffic Management Bureau, launched the Peony Traffic IC Card business. Because the card had many functions and high technological content, ICBC Beijing Branch decided to charge a card issuance fee based on its high card production costs and other actual circumstances. This decision did not violate the laws and regulations in effect at that time. The Measures for the Administration of the Application and Charges of Integrated Circuit Cards, formulated by the National Development and Reform Commission and other departments, came into effect on September 28, 2001. The plaintiff Yu Shanlan argued that the fee decision of ICBC Beijing Branch violated Articles 7, 8, and 9 of the Measures for the Administration of the Application and Charges of Integrated Circuit Cards and requested the court to order ICBC Beijing Branch to immediately cease implementing the fee standard it had formulated. This argument was not sustainable.

Accordingly, on July 26, 2004, the Xuanwu District People's Court of Beijing rendered judgment:

Rejected all claims of the plaintiff Yu Shanlan.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 50, to be borne by the plaintiff Yu Shanlan, payable within seven days from the effective date of this judgment.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, Yu Shanlan appealed to the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, arguing: The Measures for the Administration of the Application and Charges of Integrated Circuit Cards provide clear rules on fees for IC cards, and the fees for Peony Traffic IC Cards should comply with these rules. The first-instance judgment had unclear factual findings and erroneous application of law. He requested the court to set aside the first-instance judgment and enter judgment in favor of the claims he had made in the first instance.

The respondent ICBC Xuanwu Sub-branch and the respondent ICBC Beijing Branch agreed with the first-instance judgment.

The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court found through trial:

On September 28, 2001, the State Planning Commission, the National Golden Card Project Coordination Leading Group, the Ministry of Finance, and the People's Bank of China formulated the Measures for the Administration of the Application and Charges of Integrated Circuit Cards. Article 7 of the Measures provides: "Where an administrative organ implements administrative management and promotes the use of IC cards to improve management efficiency and facilitate service recipients, it may charge users according to approved standards. The charging items shall be submitted to the Ministry of Finance and the State Planning Commission or the provincial, autonomous region, or municipal finance and price departments for approval according to the attribution relationship, and the charging standards shall be submitted to the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance or the provincial, autonomous region, or municipal price and finance departments for verification." Article 9 provides: "Where a financial enterprise jointly issues IC cards with an administrative organ, the provisions of Article 7 of these Measures shall apply." Article 10 provides: "For IC cards for which charging is approved and for IC cards that are not separately charged according to regulations, if a replacement card is required due to loss, damage, or other reasons, the fee shall be charged based on the production cost of the IC card."

During the second-instance trial, the respondent ICBC Beijing Branch submitted evidence showing that the production cost of each Peony Traffic IC card was RMB 30.80. The appellant Yu Shanlan did not object to the production cost but argued that the fee for replacement cards must be approved; otherwise, no fee may be charged.

Apart from the above, the second instance confirmed the other facts found in the first instance.

The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held:

The Peony Traffic IC Card Replacement Notice Form signed by the appellant Yu Shanlan and the Baizhifang Savings Office was lawful and valid, and both parties should comply with it. The notice form did not stipulate a fee for the replacement card; therefore, Yu Shanlan's signature did not mean that he had to accept the price of RMB 100 per replacement card. The Peony Traffic IC Card is an integrated circuit card jointly issued by the Beijing Traffic Management Bureau, for the management of motor vehicle drivers in the city, and the respondent ICBC Beijing Branch. Although the card was issued before the implementation of the Measures for the Administration of the Application and Charges of Integrated Circuit Cards, after the Measures came into effect, the replacement card fee for the Peony Traffic IC Card should be determined in accordance with Articles 7, 9, and 10 of the Measures, i.e., it should be charged based on the production cost of the IC card. According to the evidence presented by ICBC Beijing Branch, the production cost of each Peony Traffic IC card was RMB 30.80, while the fee charged by the branch for replacement cards was RMB 100 per card. For the excess of RMB 69.20, ICBC Beijing Branch could not provide a legal basis. Pursuant to Article 92 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, this RMB 69.20 constitutes unjust enrichment and shall be returned by the collecting party to the payer. Yu Shanlan's request to order the respondent ICBC Xuanwu Sub-branch to return the full RMB 100 replacement card fee and interest could not be fully upheld. His request to order ICBC Beijing Branch to immediately cease implementing the fee standard it had formulated and to submit the fee standard for replacement Peony Traffic IC cards to the Beijing price authority for approval in accordance with the relevant provisions does not fall within the scope of this case and was not addressed.

Accordingly, on January 25, 2005, the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item 3 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered judgment:

1. The first-instance civil judgment was set aside.
2. Within seven days after this judgment takes effect, the respondent ICBC Xuanwu Sub-branch shall return to the appellant Yu Shanlan RMB 69.20 as the replacement card fee and interest (the interest, calculated from July 31, 2003, to the date of this judgment, based on the principal of RMB 69.20 and at the current deposit interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period).
3. The remaining claims of the appellant Yu Shanlan were rejected.

Court acceptance fees for the first and second instances, each RMB 50, shall be borne by the respondent ICBC Xuanwu Sub-branch.
